title: Tenant SLA lanes and cost-bucket spec for enterprise reporting requests
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define and implement SLA-aware request lanes and tenant-level cost buckets for enterprise console reporting requests. The goal is to provide deterministic delivery windows, predictable cost attribution, and automated gating for large exports and analytics queries requested via the Console or support flows.
background: Enterprise customers repeatedly request stronger delivery guarantees for scheduled data exports and ad-hoc analytics queries. Currently exports are single global queue with soft prioritization; large exports can cause spikes that affect latency for interactive dashboards and cross-tenant cost unpredictability. We need a non-disruptive approach that surfaces contract-driven expectations and enforces sensible cost controls without blocking self-serve usage for most teams.
problem_statement: No SLA differentiation for reporting/exports: (1) lack of explicit lanes tied to contract tiers causes unpredictable delivery windows; (2) per-tenant cost attribution for exports is coarse — this makes it hard to bill or recommend dedicated capacity; (3) Console lacks UX affordances to communicate expected wait times and cost impact for large requests.
proposed_solution:
Introduce three export lanes mapped to contract tiers: Gold (SLA: 2 hours), Silver (SLA: 8 hours), Bronze (best-effort within 48 hours). Each tenant has a configurable cost bucket used for chargeback and quota evaluation. Implementation pieces:
- Control-plane: lane assignment based on tenant contract metadata + manual override.
- Routing: separate worker queues with capacity limits and throttles.
- Quotas & guardrails: per-tenant export cost budget evaluated at request submission; >budget prompts a confirmation modal in Console or an email for support.
- Console UX: show lane, ETA, estimated token/compute cost, and a confirmation flow for heavy exports.
- Observability: per-lane metrics (queue depth, median RTT, failures) and cost attribution tags for billing export pipeline.
- Rollout approach: opt-in beta for selected enterprise tenants, collect SLO telemetry, then open to all via tenant settings.
tradeoffs: Pros: predictable SLAs for enterprise customers; clearer signal for when to recommend Dedicated; improved billing accuracy for exports.
Cons: increased operational complexity (multiple queues) and potential higher infra costs; risk of over-promising if worker capacity not scaled appropriately.

Mitigations: start with conservative capacity limits, implement automated fallbacks to Bronze lane when capacity constrained, and build a circuit-breaker that rejects exports exceeding absolute system-wide limits.
Scope decision: MVP excludes per-route traffic-splitting and fine-grained persistent preemption; those can be added once lane behavior is validated.
rollout_plan: 2) Backend: implement lane metadata on tenant object, queue routing, basic quota checks (2 sprints).
3) Console: UX for lane selection & confirmation modal, ETA calc (1 sprint parallel).
4) Observability: dashboards for lane health and cost tags (0.5 sprint).
5) Beta: invite 5 enterprise tenants for 4 weeks, run weekly SLO reviews.
6) Post-beta: iterate on capacity and automated scaling rules, then GA with tenant opt-in settings.
acceptance_criteria: - Tenant can be assigned a lane (Gold/Silver/Bronze) via admin UI or contract metadata.
- Console shows lane, ETA, and estimated compute cost before export confirmation.
- Export routing uses distinct queues and honors SLA targets for median completion in beta tenants.
- Cost attribution tags are present on all export jobs and are visible in the billing export.
- Guardrail triggers a confirmation or rejection when tenant export would exceed cost bucket budget.
- Observability dashboard surfaces queue depth and SLO breach alerts per lane.
- Security review completed and sign-off recorded.
- Post-beta report with SLO attainment, infra cost delta, and customer feedback collected.
